The Prophet would not enter over a cushion with pictures Aisha bought, saying picture-makers will be told to give them life and angels do not enter houses with pictures.
The Prophet tore Aisha's curtain decorated with pictures, and she made it into two cushions that he sat on.
Angels do not enter a house with pictures or a dog; picture-makers will be punished, the Prophet tells Aisha over a pictured pillow; Zaid excepts embroidery on garments.
Holding a tuft of hair, Muawiya said the Prophet forbade false hair, saying the Israelites were destroyed when their women used it.
On his last visit to Medina Muawiya showed a tuft of false hair in a sermon, saying the Prophet called the practice falsehood.
Ibn Mas'ud curses women who tattoo, pluck facial hair or space their teeth, as the Prophet did, citing verse 59.7, and the Prophet cursed women using false hair.
The Prophet will not enter where Aisha placed a cushion with pictures, saying picture-makers will be punished and angels do not enter a house with pictures.
The Prophet forbade gold rings; he threw away the gold ring he had made, saying he would never wear it, and wore a silver ring, its stone silver too.
A silver ring the Prophet had engraved 'Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah' sealed his letters, and Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman wore it until it fell into Aris well.
The Prophet had too few grey hairs to dye; Um Salama kept some of his reddish dyed hair; Jews and Christians do not dye, so do otherwise.
The Prophet first let his hair hang down like the people of the Scripture, not parted like the pagans', then parted it; Aisha recalled its parting shining in Ihram.
The Prophet forbade Al-Qaza', shaving a boy's head while leaving tufts of hair here and there, as Nafi' explained.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with her own hands for Ihram and at Mina before Tawaf al-Ifada, with the best scent, until its shine showed on his head and beard.
Aisha combed the Prophet's hair during her periods, and he liked to start from the right in combing and in ablution.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with the best scent before Ihram, and with Dharira at the Farewell Hajj on entering and leaving it, and he never refused a gift of scent.
Allah cursed women who tattoo, remove facial hair, gap their teeth or add false hair, or have it done, false hair being refused even for a bride who lost hers.
The Prophet forbade tattooing and cursed women who tattoo, are tattooed or lengthen hair, as he forbade usury and the price of blood or a dog; Umar asked about it.
Angels do not enter a house with a dog or pictures; picture-makers face the severest punishment and must give life to their work, and the Prophet tore Aisha's pictured curtain.
Seeing Aisha's pictured cushion the Prophet would not enter, saying picture-makers must give life to their work and angels avoid such houses, though a design on a garment is excepted.
The Prophet threw away the gold ring he wore with its stone inward, swearing never to wear it, and the people threw away their rings too.
To write to the Byzantines, who read only sealed letters, the Prophet took a silver ring engraved 'Muhammad, Apostle of Allah'.
Picture-makers will be punished on Resurrection and told to give life to what they made; Allah challenges those imitating His creation to create an ant or a grain.
